text:
morgan: Heads up — we're seeing a small spike of 403s when users switch projects immediately after an org-level API key rotation. Report from a customer in EU region.

 tanya: got an example request/response?

 morgan: pasted below (redacted):

 morgan: POST /v1/projects/switch
 morgan: Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***

 morgan: Response: 403 Forbidden
 morgan: body: {"error":"insufficient_scope","message":"project:access denied"}

 jordan: that's odd — rotation should rotate key metadata not scopes. Which token type is this? user vs service?

 devops-oncall: looks like token was a delegated service token. I see a rotation job at 2024-11-05T14:03:12Z that updated key metadata and emitted sessions:claim-trim events for that org.

 session-bot: event: sessions:claim-trim org_id=org-123 reason=api_key_rotation

 morgan: customer reports they didn't fully log out of the console; they clicked org switch and immediately got 403.

 tanya: repro steps request: 1) create delegated key scoped to projects:* 2) login as user in console 3) rotate key via org settings 4) switch org in console — confirm 403

 jordan: suspect cached session still has old claims but auth server trimmed claims on rotation. Console uses client-side cached session claim map and doesn't force refresh on org switch.

 devops-oncall: quick mitigation: instruct affected users to sign out and sign back in; that forces a new session with fresh claims. Longer term we should: 1) detect sessions:claim-trim events and trigger session refresh for active console clients 2) show a banner "please re-authenticate" on org switch if session claims mismatch.

 morgan: customer wants guidance — I'll send the sign-out workaround now and open a ticket for automatic refresh.

 tanya: I'll add a small handler to the auth bridge to emit a websocket "claims_changed" event for active sessions when claim-trim occurs. Should be low-risk.

 jordan: also add a small metric for "org_switch_403_after_rotation" so we can quantify.

 morgan: thanks — will follow up with customer once we have mitigation plan. :thumbsup:
